prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No open or discoverable system designs a custom crop variety for any field in weeks, so the Main KPI of 500,000,000 farmers with a field-tuned variety is unmet. AI breeding companies predict performance of untested combinations in silico (Inari, Computomics, Heritable Agriculture, Wild Bioscience, DNA Harvest Partners with ToolGen, https://www.htgf.de/en/computomics-interview/), but the fastest reported timelines are months for selection stages at Bayer (four to six months instead of five to six years) and about four years from start to shelf for a Heritable Ag strawberry (https://agfundernews.com/digital-twins-heritable-ag-combines-ai-genomics-and-environmental-data-to-slash-rd-timelines). Variety development still takes 8 to 15 years including multi-environment trials, and speed breeding projects six to seven years for peanut (https://wildpeanutlab.uga.edu/files/2019/06/2019-Hickey-Breeding-crops-to-feed-10-billion_Nature-Biotech.pdf); regulatory testing remains. Envirotyping with genomic prediction is active research (57 Europe PMC records 2023-2026, for example G3 2023, Theor Appl Genet 2024) but predicts across target environments, not one field. Honest limit: genomic prediction and per-field variety recommendation from existing catalogues are known, so tasks that only re-fit published GxE prediction models or recommend among released varieties are known answers; the open work is designing and validating a new field-specific variety on a weeks timescale, and each task needs its own basis.
